answer: A memory-hard sequential proof of work is bound to a non-transferable tenure record, so the work cannot be parallelised across clones, cannot be sold to another identity, and cannot be reused, because the memory-hardness forces one sequential chain per identity. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. The onyx is the sequential proof, the falcon the tenure it is bound to, and the nectar the memory-hardness that resists parallel evaluation; the onyx and the falcon are per identity, and it is the nectar that stops one proof serving a hundred clones.
